ruling.recommended_action: Refer the case file to Trust & Safety for human review of the alleged threat; do not issue any fare adjustment. Include both chat messages, the driver's written statement, and the trip GPS/timeline summary for the reviewer.
ruling.reasoning:
This case was filed by the driver as a safety incident [F1] and the trace marks SAFE-1 as satisfied, so no automatic ruling is available and the court's role is limited to gathering evidence and preparing the case file. The dispute turns entirely on the content of the exchange, which I have read in full.

The timestamps place the incident inside the trip: Chat #1 at 08:42 driver: "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3]; Chat #2 at 08:43 rider: "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4]. The driver's written statement after the trip repeats that he asked the passenger politely not to smoke, that the rider said he would punch him if he said it again, and that he kept driving and did not answer [F6]. Both messages are timestamped and part of the two-message chat record [F5], so nothing about the exchange's timing or authorship is in doubt.

There is no route or fare issue to decide: actual distance equals the optimal route at 8.5 km (+0.0 km) [F1], so no deviation arises under RD-1/RD-2, and the fare was metered [F1]. The profile entries — rider 735 days, rating 4.5, no disputes or upheld breaches [F7]; driver 1974 days, rating 4.82, 743 trips, no disputes [F8] — are context only and decide nothing.

A threat of physical violence aimed at the driver, made in the in-app chat during the trip, is a threat/harassment indicator under SAFE-1 §5.2. Accordingly the safety screen is "confirmed", and under SAFE-3 §5.2 I may summarise and prepare the file but may not assign fault or recommend an outcome. For the reviewer: the disputed question is whether the rider's message was a genuine threat of assault and whether any rider-account action is warranted; the facts to check are F3, F4, F5 (timestamps) and F6 (driver's account, which is his claim). [F4], sent during the trip after the driver's no-smoking request [F3], is a threat of physical violence requiring human review under SAFE-1 / SAFE-3; the system may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on safety incidents.
